title: ‘God does not will to punish’ is ambiguous—actual remission vs decree to transfer into a non-punishable state
source_text: XVI. At, inquies, cujuscunque Deus peccata punire non vult, peccata illi actu remissa sunt. Sed Deus ab aeterno non vult electorum peccata punire. Ergo electis ab aeterno peccata actu remissa sunt. Respondeo illam propositionem, Cujuscunque Deus non vult peccata punire, peccata illi actu remissa sunt, aut falsam esse, aut saltem veram solum cum distinctione. Nam duobus modis dicitur Deus nolle peccata alicujus punire. Et primo quidem, quoniam aliquis est in eo statu, in quo secundum ordinem a Deo constitutum, peccata hominis punienda non sunt. Sic Deus punire non vult peccata hominis cujus peccati poenitet, & qui Christum fide amplectitur, quia secundum ordinem a Deo constitutum, peccata hominis credentis & poenitentis punienda non sunt. Et cui Deus peccata hoc sensu punire non vult, peccata illi actu remissa sunt. Secundo dici potest Deus nolle peccata alicujus punire, quia decrevit illum in eum statum transferre, in quo secundum divinae justitiae ordinem, peccata ejus amplius punienda non erunt, licet nondum actu sit in eum statum translatus. Sic Deus nolebat punire peccata Pauli ante conversionem, quia decreverat illum per gratiam suam immutare, & efficere ut Christum, quem tum persequebatur, vera vivaque fide amplecteretur, qua ratione illum ex eo statu erepturus erat, in quo damnationi aeternae subjacebat. Falsum est autem actu remissa esse peccata illi, cujus hoc sensu & modo duntaxat Deus dicitur nolle peccata punire. Quia ille quem Deus in statum gratiae transferre decrevit, potest adhuc aliquantisper in statu perditionis haerere. Qui autem est adhuc in statu mortis & perditionis, nondum illi actu peccata remissa sunt. Uno verbo, cujuscunque Deus non vult peccata punire, peccata illi vel actu remissa sunt, si priore modo Deus ea punire nolit: Vel aliquando saltem remittenda, si solum Deus ea punire nolit posteriori modo.
pass_a_gloss: But, you will say: whoever’s sins God does not will to punish, those sins are actually remitted to him. But God from eternity does not will to punish the elect’s sins. Therefore to the elect from eternity sins are actually remitted. I answer that that proposition—Whoever’s sins God does not will to punish, those sins are actually remitted to him—is either false, or at least true only with a distinction. For God is said in two ways not to will to punish someone’s sins. And first indeed, because someone is in that state in which, according to the order constituted by God, a man’s sins are not to be punished. Thus God does not will to punish the sins of a man who repents of sin and who embraces Christ by faith, because according to the order constituted by God the sins of a believing and repentant man are not to be punished. And to him whose sins God in this sense does not will to punish, sins are actually remitted. Second, God can be said not to will to punish someone’s sins because he has decreed to transfer him into that state in which, according to the order of divine justice, his sins will no longer be to be punished, although he has not yet actually been transferred into that state. Thus God was unwilling to punish Paul’s sins before conversion, because he had decreed to change him by his grace and to bring it about that he would embrace with true and living faith the Christ whom he then persecuted, by which means he was going to snatch him from that state in which he lay under eternal damnation. But it is false that sins are actually remitted to him of whom God is said only in this sense and manner not to will to punish sins. Because he whom God has decreed to transfer into the state of grace can still for a while cling in the state of perdition. But he who is still in the state of death and perdition does not yet have sins actually remitted to him. In a word: whoever’s sins God does not will to punish, those sins are either actually remitted to him, if God is unwilling to punish them in the former way; or at least someday to be remitted, if God is unwilling to punish them only in the latter way.
pass_b_english: ‘God will not punish’ splits: (1) already in the faith-repentance order → actual remission; (2) only decreed to be moved there → not yet.
Paul pre-conversion shows decree-not-to-punish without actual pardon while still in perdition.
